gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-glegoo: Friendly and striking, Lemon Milk spaces its rounded, single-width letters wide apart, while Glegoo's serif body keeps its tall lowercase and open curves. They sit together easily.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-hanuman: Loose, wide and cheerfully round, Lemon Milk draws every stroke the same thickness. Hanuman, a text serif with a high-waisted lowercase, gives the pair its strongest quality: a heading and body that genuinely differ.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-kadwa: Kadwa reads large and classic, its serif lowercase tall and its curves left open at the ends. And Lemon Milk handles the loud, hairline-free heading work while Kadwa does the steady talking.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-noticia-text: Lemon Milk spreads its rounded letters wide, like neatly bent pipe cleaner, and that gives the heading a friendly, striking face. Noticia Text answers with literary serif calm.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla reads as a classic serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, with an e that opens wide. Lemon Milk is the one to stand out, while Piazzolla carries the words.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-pridi: Lemon Milk comes first, wide-tracked and rounded, with no thick and thin parts anywhere. Pridi, a classic serif with small letters standing almost capital-sized, is the one that settles in and does the careful reading work.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-scope-one: Lemon Milk keeps every line the same width. Scope One then plays the opposite part as a serif, with a big x-height, stubby ascenders and counters that spill into the space around them.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-slabo-13px: Wire-bent and wide-spaced, Lemon Milk greets you with friendly, striking rounded letters, then hands over to Slabo 13px. That serif feels bookish and dignified beside it.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-gf-suwannaphum: Suwannaphum reads tall and dignified, its serif x-height lifted high and its c wide open. And Lemon Milk's wide, rounded heading letters keep that long body text from feeling stiff.
gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-domine: Domine reads like a refined serif, compact above and tall in the lowercase. Nasalization's friendly floating letters and thick crossbars give the pair its strongest quality: a heading that loosens up a dignified body.
